title: What can be tailored and what cannot
blurb: Sort proposed changes into acceptable tailoring and changes that break a principle or a role rule.
question: A project manager proposes renaming stages as 'phases', letting project support also carry out project assurance, and holding highlight reporting online. Which of these are acceptable tailoring?

teach.h: Five things flex, one thing does not
teach.body: Formally, PRINCE2 lets a project tailor its processes, its practices (through the management approaches), its roles, its management products and its terminology. The principles cannot be tailored, and the rules about roles still apply. In plain English: you can change how the method works, who wears which hat, what the documents look like and what things are called, but you cannot skip a principle or break the rules that keep governance safe.

teach.caption: Every choice is documented and agreed, and recorded in the project initiation documentation (PID).

teach.h: The numbers that do not move

items.label: principles, all applied on every project
executive, not combined with the PM
aspects of the method you can tailor

teach.body: The seven principles are the guiding obligations that make a project a PRINCE2 project. If any principle is not applied, the project is not using PRINCE2, however carefully everything else is tailored. That is why tailoring decisions can change processes, practices, roles, products and terms, but never the principles.

teach.caption: Roles can be combined, split or added, but within these rules. Senior user and senior supplier may each be more than one person.

teach.body: The practices are tailored mainly through the nine management approaches agreed in initiation: benefits, change, commercial, communication, digital and data, issue, quality, risk and sustainability. A small project might use a short risk management approach and informal issue handling; a large one might need fuller versions. The practice still applies; its approach is scaled.

children.edge: Changes how an element is applied
children.label: Tailoring: document in PID

teach.body: At Saltmarsh Housing Association, project manager Grace Whitfield is upgrading door-entry systems in 12 blocks. She proposes calling work packages 'job packs', acting as team manager herself, and using a one-page highlight format. All three are tailoring. A board member then suggests skipping lessons to save time, and the finance director offers to be executive and project manager. Grace explains both are refused: one drops a principle, the other breaks a role rule.

teach.text: Changing terms, merging documents, adding a coach role or adjusting how often and how formally reports are produced is tailoring. Omitting a principle, combining the executive and project manager, or putting project assurance with the project manager or project support is not.

items: Tailorable: processes, practices (via management approaches), roles, management products and terminology.
Role rules still apply: one executive; executive and PM not combined; PM role not shared; assurance independent of the PM.
Roles can be combined, split or added, for example adding a coach.
Products can be merged, split, renamed or reformatted.

summary: You can now name the five things PRINCE2 lets you tailor (processes, practices through management approaches, roles, management products and terminology) and explain why the principles cannot be tailored. You can also spot role changes that break the rules, such as combining executive and project manager.

A.q: Which can be tailored on a PRINCE2 project?
options: The seven principles
The management products
The rule of one executive
Assurance independence
A.why: Management products can be merged, split, renamed or given different formats when tailoring (2.7).

whyNot.0: Principles cannot be tailored; all seven must be applied.
whyNot.2: There must be one executive; this role rule still applies when tailoring.
whyNot.3: Project assurance must stay independent of the project manager; tailoring does not change that.

A.q: How are the PRINCE2 practices tailored to suit a project?
options: Through the mandate from the business
Through lessons reports from past projects
Through the daily log kept by the PM
Through the management approaches
A.why: Practices are tailored through the management approaches agreed during initiation (2.7, 15.4.2).

whyNot.0: The mandate comes from the business layer to trigger the project; it does not tailor the practices.
whyNot.1: The lessons report passes on lessons at the end of a stage or project; it does not set how practices apply.
whyNot.2: The daily log is the project manager's informal diary of actions and minor issues.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. On a PRINCE2 project, the [?] cannot be tailored, although the way the method is applied can be.
options: principles
processes
roles
terminology
A.why: The principles cannot be tailored; processes, practices, roles, management products and terminology can (2.7).

whyNot.1: Processes can be tailored: combined, simplified or carried out in more detail.
whyNot.2: Roles can be tailored: combined, split or added, within the role rules.
whyNot.3: Terminology can be tailored to the organization's own terms.

B.q:
Which two are acceptable ways of tailoring roles?
1. Adding a coach to help teams work with a supplier's agile method.
2. Letting the project manager also perform the team manager role.
3. Sharing the executive role between two directors.
4. Giving project assurance to project support.
options: 1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
1 and 2
B.why: Roles may be added (such as a coach) and combined within the rules (the PM may also be team manager) (2.7, 6.2.4).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is false: there is one executive, and the role is not shared.
whyNot.1: Statement 4 is false: project support must be kept separate from project assurance.
whyNot.2: Both are false: one executive only, and assurance cannot be held by project support.

B.q: To save time, a board member suggests the project should stop checking whether the business case is still valid. What is the problem with this?
options: It is tailoring, so the business layer must approve it
It changes a product, so the PM must approve it first
It drops a principle, so the project is not PRINCE2
It is acceptable on a project within a programme
B.why: Checking that the business case remains valid is the 'ensure continued business justification' principle. Dropping it means the project is no longer PRINCE2 (ch 2, 2.1).

whyNot.0: This is not tailoring at all: principles cannot be tailored, so no one can approve dropping one.
whyNot.1: The issue is a principle, not a product, and the PM cannot approve dropping a principle either.
whyNot.3: Projects within a programme still apply all seven principles.

B.q: Which statement about tailoring management products is correct?
options: They can be merged, split, renamed or reformatted
They keep their PRINCE2 names so others recognize them
They stay fixed while processes and roles change
They are tailored by each team manager per work package
B.why: Management products can be merged, split, renamed or given different formats to suit the project (2.7).

whyNot.1: Products can be renamed; terminology can follow the organization's own terms.
whyNot.2: Management products are one of the five things that can be tailored, alongside processes and roles.
whyNot.3: Tailoring is agreed for the project in initiation, led by the project manager, and approved by the board in the PID.

C.q: A project manager proposes three changes: (1) renaming 'stages' as 'phases', (2) combining the executive and project manager roles, (3) holding highlight reporting online. Which statement is correct?
options: All three are acceptable once the PID records them
1 is tailoring; 2 and 3 break PRINCE2 role rules
1 and 3 are tailoring; 2 breaks a role rule
3 is tailoring; 1 changes a PRINCE2 principle
C.why: Renaming terms and changing reporting format are tailoring; the executive and project manager roles cannot be combined (2.7, 6.2.4).

whyNot.0: Recording a change in the PID cannot make a broken role rule acceptable.
whyNot.1: Online highlight reporting changes the format of a report; it involves no role.
whyNot.3: Renaming terms is tailoring terminology, not a change to a principle.

C.q: Which role arrangement is allowed when tailoring a PRINCE2 project?
options: Project assurance carried out by project support
The executive role shared by two directors
Project support provided by team members
The PM role split between two managers
C.why: Project support can be delegated, for example to a PMO, suppliers or team members (6.2.4).

whyNot.0: Project support must be kept separate from project assurance.
whyNot.1: There is one executive; the role is not shared.
whyNot.3: The project manager role should not be shared, so that it has a single focus.

C.q: A supplier's quality system means the project will add some extra quality records and rename two of its reports. Which elements are being tailored?
options: Principles and quality processes
Management products and terminology
Roles and the seven principles
Processes and project board roles
C.why: Adding records and renaming reports change the management products and the terminology, both of which can be tailored (2.7).

whyNot.0: Principles cannot be tailored, and no process is changing here.
whyNot.2: No role is changing, and principles cannot be tailored.
whyNot.3: The change is to documents and names, not to processes or roles.

reteach.title: Movable walls, fixed foundations
reteach.question: In a house, you can move internal walls, rename rooms and change the furniture, but not remove the foundations. Which parts of PRINCE2 are the walls, and which are the foundations?

blocks.body: The movable walls are the processes, practices, roles, management products and terminology: rearrange them to suit the household. The foundations are the seven principles. The building regulations are the role rules: one executive, executive and project manager kept apart, project manager role not shared, assurance independent of the project manager.

blocks.text: A role change can look like tailoring and still be wrong. Combining executive and project manager, or giving assurance to the project manager or project support, breaks the role rules.

explain.body: Processes can be combined, simplified or carried out in more detail. What does not change is that the board's decision points still happen: for example, delivery does not start before the board authorizes the project.

test.q: Which is a valid way to tailor a PRINCE2 process?
options: Simplify it to suit a small, simple project
Start delivery before the PID is authorized
Let a team manager authorize the next stage
Replace board decisions with PM approvals
test.why: Processes can be combined, simplified or done in more detail to suit the project (2.7).

whyNot.1: Starting delivery before the board authorizes the project skips a decision point; that is not tailoring.
whyNot.2: Authorizing a stage is a project board decision in directing a project.
whyNot.3: Board decisions are part of governance and stay with the board.

explain.body: Practices are tailored through their management approaches. A low-risk project might use a brief risk management approach; a complex one a detailed approach.

test.q: A low-risk project uses a short, simple risk management approach. What is being tailored?
options: A principle, through the risk appetite
A role, through its role description
A process, through its activities
A practice, through its approach
test.why: Practices are tailored through their management approaches; here the risk practice is scaled through the risk management approach (2.7).

whyNot.0: Principles cannot be tailored, and risk appetite is set by the business, not by tailoring.
whyNot.1: No role description is changing; the change is to how risk is managed.
whyNot.2: The change is to the risk management approach, not to process activities.

explain.body: Roles can be combined, split or added. The PM may also be team manager and project support. But the executive cannot be combined with the PM, and assurance cannot be held by the PM, team members or project support.

test.q: Which tailoring of roles breaks a PRINCE2 rule?
options: The PM also acts as team manager
Two senior users represent two user groups
The PM also carries out project assurance
Project support comes from a PMO
test.why: Project assurance cannot be assigned to the project manager; it must be independent of the PM (6.2.4).

whyNot.0: Depending on scale and capacity, the PM may also perform the team manager role.
whyNot.1: The senior user role can be held by more than one person.
whyNot.3: Project support can be provided by a PMO.

explain.body: Management products can be merged, split, renamed or reformatted, and PRINCE2 terms can be replaced with those the organization already uses.

test.q: An organization calls its highlight report a 'monthly board note'. What is this?
options: A breach of the progress practice
Tailoring terminology to the organization
A change that needs an exception report
A new product outside the PRINCE2 method
test.why: Using the organization's own names for PRINCE2 products is tailoring of terminology (2.7).

whyNot.0: The progress practice still applies; only the report's name differs.
whyNot.2: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of stage tolerance, not for renaming.
whyNot.3: It is the same highlight report under the organization's name, not a new product.
